title: FP8 profile sanity & prompt-suite QA for Hopper E4M3/E5M2
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Validate and harden the FP8 quantization profiles for Hopper GPUs (E4M3/E5M2) by running a comprehensive prompt-suite QA, adding automated sanitization checks to the calibration pipeline, and shipping a short-term stability shim that prevents noisy per-op scale activations from propagating into production.

Scope:
- Add a lightweight "sanitization" pass to the calibration pipeline that checks per-op scale distributions across a seed sweep and clamps outliers for known problematic ops.
- Expand the golden prompt-suite with 120 new short/long prompts covering instruction-following, coding, math, and safety edge cases.
- Run differential accuracy and regression tests vs FP32 and INT8 baselines; flag any prompt with >0.75% accuracy drop or any semantic token shifts.
- Instrument telemetry and automatic gating: if instability seen in 0.1% of requests in shadow, block rollout and alert SRE/Model-ops.

Non-goals: Interpreting model architecture changes or retraining; this ticket is strictly calibration/validation and rollout automation.

Why this is different: Previous work focused on selector heuristics and long-running calibration services. This ticket targets an orthogonal problem: noisy per-op scale spikes during FP8 activation on Hopper that cause rare but high-severity output divergence. We introduce deterministic sanitization rules plus an expanded prompt-suite to surface these rare regressions earlier.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Spike: ran seed sweep (n=8 seeds) for base-7B on E4M3 profile; observed 0.9% semantic drift on 6/120 prompts concentrated on code-completion samples. Logs captured per-op scale spikes on 'mlp_fc_out' and 'proj_out'.

2025-02-13 - Decision: add sanitization clamp in calibration that enforces per-op mean/variance window and rejects profiles with ops exceeding 6 sigma from historical baseline. Agreed in triage with @SRE and @ModelOps. Action: Marco to prototype clamp shim.

2025-02-15 - Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1893 created (fp8: sanitization pass + CLI flag --fp8-sanitize). Initial unit tests included. Requesting eng review from @J. Kim and @L. O'Malley.

2025-02-18 - Run: Expanded prompt-suite to 240 total prompts (added heavy-code and instruction-mix). Shadow run on dedicated pool showed regressions reduced to 0.18% with sanitization enabled. Latency regression measured at +2.7% p50, CPU overhead negligible. Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/quant/fp8-sanity-2025-02

2025-02-20 - PR review feedback: add deterministic seed control in calibration harness to eliminate seed drift, and add README for operators describing when to opt-out (edge cases: extreme long context (>16k) and very low token diversity workloads).

2025-02-24 - Canaries: plan drafted — Shadow -> 1% canary -> 5% canary -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on accuracy gate. See rollout doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Fp8+Sanitization+Runbook

2025-02-27 - QA: synthetic adversarial prompts were added to surface scale oscillations; two prompts still tripped the 0.75% threshold on E5M2 in extreme token-length cases. Next: extend clamp to include hysteresis window across sequence length bins.
acceptance_criteria: Sanitization pass merged and enabled behind feature-flag --fp8-sanitize
Golden prompt-suite baseline: no more than 0.5% of prompts exceed 0.75% relative drop vs FP32 baseline across 10 seed sweep
Latency P50 regression due to sanitization < 5% for target models on Hopper; memory overhead measured and documented
Automated telemetry alerts configured: accuracy_regression_rate, per_op_scale_outlier_rate, and shadow_fail_rate
Rollout playbook validated with a dry-run and automated rollback on accuracy gate
telemetry_checks: accuracy_regression_rate (fraction of prompts with semantic divergence) - threshold 0.0075
shadow_fail_rate (requests failing golden-suite in shadow) - trigger > 0.005
p50/p90 latency delta vs baseline - trigger p50 > 1.10 or p90 > 1.15
kv_cache_mismatch_count - alert if > 10 in a five minute window
test_plan: 1) Local calibration run with --fp8-sanitize enabled across seed sweep n=10 for base-7B and base-34B on both E4M3 and E5M2 images
2) Run differential eval: compare outputs to FP32 and INT8 golden outputs using semantic matching and token-level diffs; generate per-prompt delta report
3) Run stress harness on long-context scenarios (8k, 16k, 32k tokens) to validate hysteresis behavior
4) Shadow run on Dedicated pool for 48 hours with mixed traffic and logging enabled
5) Canary rollout with progressive weights and automated gating, followed by full rollout if gates pass
rollout_plan: Shadow (0%) for 48h -> evaluate telemetry and prompt-suite failures
Canary 1% traffic for 4h -> automatic accuracy gate check
Canary 5% for 12h -> manual inspection of flagged prompts by ModelOps
Canary 25% for 24h -> if stable, ramp to 100% over next 6h
Automated rollback: any gate breach triggers immediate reroute to INT8 variant and rollback to previous profile version
